definitions.explanation: Casual, internet-flavored slang for an outstanding, deeply moving song — a "god-tier tune." Formed from {神|かみ} (god, used as an intensifier) and {曲|きょく} (musical piece).

examples.japanese: この{曲|きょく}は{神曲|しんきょく}だ。
examples.english: This song is an absolute masterpiece.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{新|あたら}しい{歌|うた}は{神曲|しんきょく}だと{話題|わだい}だ。
examples.english: Her new song is the talk of the town as a masterpiece.

examples.japanese: ライブで{神曲|しんきょく}が{続|つづ}いて{会場|かいじょう}が{盛|も}り{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: The venue got fired up as one great song after another played at the concert.

notes:
USAGE: As slang, {神曲|しんきょく} means an outstanding, unforgettable song. The prefix {神|かみ}/{神|しん} is widely used to intensify praise (compare {神|かみ}{対応|たいおう}, "god-tier response").

NOTE ON OTHER MEANING: The same characters {神曲|しんきょく} are also the Japanese title of Dante's Divine Comedy; context makes clear which is meant.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {名曲|めいきょく}: a famous, classic song — an established masterpiece, not slang
- {新曲|しんきょく}: a new song — a homophone; a newly released track
